key_insight: Symmetric splitting delivers second-order shallow-water time stepping on the sphere while restricting stability through advection rather than fast waves.
engineering_relevance: The scheme supports efficient spherical flow simulations relevant to weather and climate modelling, with advection subcycling enabling larger overall time steps without extra implicit solves.
method: Split time stepping into an explicit half-step, a full advection step, and an implicit half-step.
Advance advection with DG-upwind SSPRK3 and discretise waves implicitly using compatible finite elements.
Use hybridisation for the implicit solve while projecting velocity back into the H(div)-conforming space.
evidence_signal: Firedrake tests on standard spherical shallow-water benchmarks report second-order convergence, good parallel scaling, and stability at Courant numbers up to 1 with two advection subcycles and second-order elements.
watch_item: Advection remains CFL-limited, and larger overall time steps require subcycling; the abstract does not quantify runtime savings.
paper_title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
